script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: friendship

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. JAMES, a warm, middle-aged woman, stands at the kitchen sink, her back to the room. She gazes out the window, her face a mix of concern and determination.

MRS. JAMES
(to herself)
I've got to do something.

Suddenly, the front door swings open, and in walks LUCAS, an energetic 12-year-old boy, backpack slung over his shoulders.

LUCAS
Hey, Mom! I'm home!

Mrs. James turns to face her son, a smile playing at the corners of her mouth.

MRS. JAMES
Hello, Lucas. How was your first day at the new school?

LUCAS
It was okay, I guess. I mean, the kids seemed nice enough, but I didn't make any friends yet.

Mrs. James' face falls, and she rushes over to him, wrapping her arms around him in a hug.

MRS. JAMES
(tearfully)
Oh, sweetheart. I'm so sorry. We'll figure something out.

INT. LIVING ROOM - DAY

Lucas sits on the couch, staring at the wall, looking dejected. Mrs. James enters the room, a determined look in her eyes.

MRS. JAMES
(sitting next to Lucas)
I've got an idea. There's a community garden not far from here. Why don't you go there and meet some new friends?

LUCAS
(skeptical)
Mom, I don't even know how to garden.

MRS. JAMES
(smiling)
That's where I come in. We'll go together, and I'll teach you everything you need to know. And maybe, just maybe, you'll meet some kids your age who share the same passion for nature.

Lucas perks up at the idea.

LUCAS
Okay, Mom. I'll give it a try.

INT. COMMUNITY GARDEN - DAY

Mrs. James and Lucas arrive at the community garden. They are greeted by MR. WILSON, an older man with a friendly smile, tending to a row of tomato plants.

MR. WILSON
(smiling)
Welcome! I'm Mr. Wilson. I see you've brought a new gardener.

MRS. JAMES
Yes, this is my son, Lucas. He's new to gardening, so I'll be helping him out.

MR. WILSON
Ah, a mother-son team. That's wonderful. I'm sure you'll both learn a lot and make some new friends in the process.

INT. COMMUNITY GARDEN - AFTERNOON

Lucas and Mrs. James work side by side in the garden, planting seeds and tending to the plants. Around them, other gardeners work on their plots, some alone, some in pairs.

As the day goes on, Lucas starts to engage with the other gardeners, particularly AMY, a girl his age with an infectious enthusiasm for gardening. They share tips, swap seeds, and even laugh together.

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

Mrs. James and Lucas sit at the kitchen table, surrounded by the fruits and vegetables they've grown throughout the day.

MRS. JAMES
(smiling)
I'm so proud of you, Lucas. You've made some great strides today.

LUCAS
(grinning)
Thanks, Mom. I really had a great time at the garden. And I made a new friend, Amy.

MRS. JAMES
(pleased)
That's wonderful, sweetheart. And who knows? Maybe you'll make even more friends as the season goes on.

INT. COMMUNITY GARDEN - WEEKS LATER

The garden is thriving, and so is Lucas's friendship with Amy. They work together, plant and harvest, and even help other gardeners when they can.

One day, as they sit on the garden bench, enjoying the sun and their accomplishments, Lucas turns to Amy with a thoughtful expression.

LUCAS
You know, Amy, I think this is the best summer I've ever had.

AMY
(smiling)
Me too, Lucas. And it's all because of this garden and our friendship.

Lucas nods, his eyes shining with happiness.

LUCAS
Yeah, you're right. And I wouldn't have it any other way.

Fade to black.

THE END
